title: The Church beside the city assembly
source_text: Ἐκκλησία μὲν γὰρ τοῦ θεοῦ, φέρ᾿ εἰπεῖν, ἡ Ἀθήνῃσι πρᾳεῖά τις καὶ εὐσταθὴς, ἅτε θεῷ ἀρέσκειν τῷ ἐπὶ πᾶσι βουλομένη· ἡ δ᾿ Ἀθηναίων ἐκκλησία στασιώδης καὶ οὐδαμῶς παραβαλλομένη τῇ ἐκεῖ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ. τὸ δ᾿ αὐτὸ ἐρεῖς περὶ ἐκκλησίας τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς ἐν Κορίνθῳ καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοῦ δήμου Κορινθίων καὶ, φέρ᾿ εἰπεῖν, περὶ ἐκκλησίας τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς ἐν Ἀλεξανδρείᾳ καὶ ἐκκλησίας τοῦ Ἀλεξανδρέων δήμου. καὶ ἐὰν εὐγνώμων ᾖ ὁ τούτου ἀκούων καὶ φιλαλήθως ἐξετάζῃ τὰ πράγματα, θαυμάσεται τὸν καὶ βουλευσάμενον καὶ ἀνύσαι δυνηθέντα πανταχοῦ συστήσασθαι ἐκκλησίας τοῦ θεοῦ, παροικούσας ἐκκλησίαις τῶν καθ᾿ ἑκάστην πόλιν δήμων. οὕτω δὲ καὶ βουλὴν ἐκκλησίας θεοῦ βουλῇ τῇ καθ᾿ ἑκάστην πόλιν συνεξετάζων εὕροις ἂν, τίνες μὲν τῆς ἐκκλησίας βουλευταὶ ἄξιοί εἰσιν, εἴ τις ἐστὶν ἐν τῷ παντὶ πόλις τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν ἐκείνῃ πολιτεύεσθαι· οἱ δὲ πανταχοῦ βουλευταὶ οὐδὲν ἄξιον τῆς ἐκ κατατάξεως ὑπεροχῆς, ἣν ὑπερέχειν δοκοῦσι τῶν πολιτῶν, φέρουσιν ἐν τοῖς ἑαυτῶν ἤθεσιν. οὕτω δὲ καὶ ἄρχοντα ἐκκλησίας ἑκάστης πόλεως ἄρχοντι τῶν ἐν τῇ πόλει συγκριτέον· ἵνα κατανοήσῃς ὅτι καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν σφόδρα ἀποτυγχανομένων βουλευτῶν καὶ ἀρχόντων ἐκκλησίας θεοῦ καὶ ῥᾳθυμότερον παρὰ τοὺς εὐτονωτέρως βιούντων οὐδὲν (??)ττον ἔστιν εὑρεῖν ὡς ἐπίπαν ὑπεροχὴν τὴν ἐν τῇ ἐπὶ τὰς ἀρετὰς προκοπῇ παρὰ τὰ ἤθη τῶν ἐν ταῖς πόλεσι βουλευόντων καὶ ἀρχόντων.
pass_a_gloss: For a church (ἐκκλησία) of God, let us say (φέρ᾿ εἰπεῖν), the one at Athens [is] gentle (πρᾷος) and stable (εὐσταθής), as wishing (βούλομαι) to please (ἀρέσκω) the God over all (ὁ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεός); but the assembly (ἐκκλησία) of the Athenians [is] factious (στασιώδης) and in no way (οὐδαμῶς) being compared (παραβάλλω) with the church of God there. The same you will say about the church of God in Corinth and the assembly of the people (δῆμος) of the Corinthians, and, let us say, about the church of God in Alexandria and the assembly of the people of the Alexandrians. And if fair-minded (εὐγνώμων) be the one hearing this and with love of truth (φιλαλήθως) examine (ἐξετάζω) the facts (πράγματα), he will marvel at (θαυμάζω) the one who both planned (βουλεύομαι) and was able to accomplish (ἀνύω) to establish (συνίστημι) everywhere churches of God, sojourning beside (παροικέω) the assemblies of the peoples in each city. So also, comparing (συνεξετάζω) the council (βουλή) of the church of God with the council in each city, you would find which councillors (βουλευταί) of the church are worthy (ἄξιοι), if there is in the universe (ἐν τῷ παντί) a city (πόλις) of God, to be citizens (πολιτεύομαι) in that one; but the councillors everywhere bring (φέρω) in their own characters (ἤθη) nothing worthy of the pre-eminence (ὑπεροχή) from appointment/rank (κατάταξις) by which they seem (δοκέω) to exceed (ὑπερέχω) the citizens. So also the ruler (ἄρχων) of the church of each city is to be compared (συγκριτέον) with the ruler of those in the city; that you may perceive (κατανοέω) that even in the case of the councillors and rulers of the church of God who very much fail (ἀποτυγχάνω) and live more slackly (ῥᾳθυμότερον) compared with (παρά) those [living] more vigorously (εὐτονωτέρως), it is nonetheless (οὐδὲν ἧττον) possible to find generally (ὡς ἐπίπαν) a superiority in the progress (προκοπή) toward the virtues (ἀρεταί) compared with the characters of those being councillors and rulers in the cities.
pass_b_english: For the church of God at Athens, let us say, is a gentle and steady body, since it wishes to please the God over all; but the assembly of the Athenians is given to faction and can in no way be compared with the church of God there. You will say the same of the church of God at Corinth and the assembly of the people of Corinth, and, let us say, of the church of God at Alexandria and the assembly of the people of Alexandria. And if the one who hears this is fair-minded and examines the facts with a love of truth, he will marvel at him who both planned and was able to bring about the founding of churches of God everywhere, churches that live as sojourners beside the assemblies of the people in each city.

So too, if you compare the council of the church of God with the council in each city, you would find that some councillors of the church are worthy to hold citizenship in the city of God, if there is such a city anywhere in the universe, while the city councillors everywhere bring, in their own characters, nothing worthy of the pre-eminence their appointment gives them, by which they seem to stand above the citizens. So too the ruler of the church in each city must be compared with the ruler of the people in that city, so that you may perceive that, even among those councillors and rulers of the church of God who fall far short, and who live more carelessly than those of more vigorous life, it is nonetheless possible to find, as a general rule, a superiority in progress toward the virtues over the characters of those who sit as councillors and rulers in the cities.

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 30 (Koetschau 3.30); the chapter continues the comparison begun in 3.29. Origen plays on ἐκκλησία as both the Christian church and the civic assembly of a Greek city; rendered ‘church’ for the Christian body and ‘assembly’ for the civic one, so the contrast stays visible in English. The staged text has a damaged word ‘οὐδὲν (??)ττον’; read as οὐδὲν ἧττον (‘nonetheless’), the only reading that fits the sense. ‘βουλή’/‘βουλευταί’ (council, councillors) and ‘ἄρχων’ (ruler) are civic terms; Origen is likely mapping the church’s council (presbyters) and ruler (bishop) onto the city’s council and magistrate, but the Greek uses only the civic words, so the English keeps them. ‘τῆς ἐκ κατατάξεως ὑπεροχῆς’ rendered ‘the pre-eminence their appointment gives them’ (κατάταξις = enrolment in an order or rank). ‘παροικούσας’ (living as sojourners beside) may echo the New Testament language of believers as sojourners (compare 1 Peter 2:11), and ‘a city of God’ may echo LXX Psalm 45:5 / 86:3 (Psalm 46:4 / 87:3 in English Bibles) or Hebrews 12:22; both are uncertain, hypothetical in form (‘if there is …’), and are not cited inline. The final purpose clause (ἵνα κατανοήσῃς …) is kept as a purpose clause (‘so that you may perceive’). ‘τίνες μὲν τῆς ἐκκλησίας βουλευταί’ is accented as an indirect question (‘which councillors’); set against ‘οἱ δὲ πανταχοῦ βουλευταί’ by μέν/δέ it is rendered ‘some councillors of the church’, which keeps Origen’s point that not every church councillor is worthy. ‘οἱ πανταχοῦ βουλευταί’ rendered ‘the city councillors everywhere’, since the preceding clause sets them against the church’s council as the council ‘in each city’.

‘living as sojourners’ moved so it plainly describes the churches (παροικούσας agrees with ἐκκλησίας), not ‘him’
‘the councillors everywhere else’ made ‘the city councillors everywhere’ (‘else’ is not in the Greek)
Restored the purpose clause ἵνα κατανοήσῃς as ‘so that you may perceive’ (was ‘Then you will perceive’, a statement)
Note added on the accent of τίνες and the ‘some councillors’ rendering
